purpose: Every port, timeout, cap and exclusion rt-observe uses. No literal of any of these lives in the code (R0). Values are grouped by the collector that reads them, so a reader can see what one panel costs.

provenance.note: A value here is chosen unless its own 'provenance' says measured or specified. A missing key is an explicit error naming the key and this file (R3), never a silent default.

bind_host.provenance: specified - .claude/rules/security.md, bind a service to a specific interface and never 0.0.0.0
bind_host.note: Loopback is shared by every process on the machine, so the bind is not an authorization boundary on its own. The session token is.

port.provenance: chosen - outside the ranges this workspace already uses (5000 Flask, 5246 Blazor, 11434 Ollama)

view.purpose: Everything the served page would otherwise hardcode. It is injected as one JSON block, so the markup carries no configured number at all (R0).

poll_ms.provenance: chosen - the per-section TTLs decide what a poll actually COSTS, so this is only how often the page asks

refresh_choices_ms.unit: milliseconds between page polls, offered as the refresh control's choices
refresh_choices_ms.provenance: chosen 2026-09-01 after the operator reported the live tab lagging - the poll was never the slow part, the per-section TTL was, so the control now sets BOTH and the fastest choice is one second

refresh_bounds_ms.unit: milliseconds - the smallest and largest refresh interval a viewer may type
refresh_bounds_ms.provenance: chosen 2026-09-01 - the operator asked to type their own value rather than pick from a list, so the list became suggestions and these are the only limits. The lower bound is a courtesy to the machine and not a safety boundary: the real protection is ttl_floor_seconds, which the server applies whatever a page asks for

context_window_tokens.unit: tokens of context window used as the DENOMINATOR of the token bar, or null for no bar at all
context_window_tokens.provenance: unset on purpose - no transcript reports the window its tokens sit in, so any number here is the operator's and not a measurement. Left null the page prints the totals and draws NO bar, because a bar relative to something arbitrary reads as fullness: measured 2026-09-01, a bar scaled to the busiest session on screen showed that session permanently full

detail_rows.unit: rows of named detail a hover panel lists before it says how many more there are
detail_rows.provenance: chosen - a hover panel is read standing up, and an edge carrying every one of 134 mirrors would be a second matrix

settle_ticks.unit: simulation ticks before the layout is considered settled
settle_ticks.provenance: chosen - enough for 18 nodes to separate; with prefers-reduced-motion these run before the first paint instead of on a frame timer

lane_pull.unit: pull toward the node's own lane, which is what keeps this a wiring diagram rather than a hairball

vertical_below_px.provenance: chosen - below this the four lanes cannot fit across the panel, so the diagram is TURNED (lanes become rows) rather than shrunk to illegibility

settle_ms.unit: milliseconds of eased movement when the diagram's shape changes
settle_ms.provenance: chosen - the layout is solved silently and only the MOVE is animated, so this is how long a box takes to travel from where it was to where it now belongs. Reported 2026-08-31: animating the solver itself, and restarting it on every poll, made the diagram impossible to follow

min_alpha.unit: kinetic energy per node below which the tick loop stops
min_alpha.provenance: chosen - the loop stops rather than running forever, so a settled page costs no frames

default.unit: seconds - the fastest a viewer may ask any section to be re-collected
default.provenance: chosen - a page asking faster than this would re-run local collectors continuously for no gain, since none of them changes within a second

usage.unit: seconds - the floor for the whole-transcript usage scan
usage.provenance: chosen - it reads every transcript end to end, so a viewer turning the refresh dial to one second must not be able to make it run every second

mcp_live.unit: seconds - the floor for the MCP roster specifically
mcp_live.provenance: specified - it is the only collector that leaves the machine, reaching 28 servers under a 45-second budget, so a viewer must NOT be able to speed it up. Its floor is its own TTL

usage.provenance: chosen - this is the only collector that reads every transcript end to end, and a week's total does not move meaningfully inside ten minutes

mirrors.provenance: chosen - a filesystem walk of a few hundred small files; cheap enough to refresh often

registry.provenance: chosen - the canonical set only changes when a definition file is edited, so it is the cheapest section to hold

progress.provenance: chosen - PROGRESS.md is appended by hand during a phase, and seeing that appear is the point of the panel

services.provenance: chosen - the local daemon and Ollama probes are cheap but not free

mcp_live.provenance: chosen - `claude mcp list` reaches the network for 28 servers, so a 2-second page poll must never trigger it

graph.provenance: chosen - the snapshot only changes when local-writer refreshes it, so polling it hard buys nothing

identity.provenance: chosen 2026-09-24 - the identity/audit layer (rt_store.py, Phase 2 of the journal-durable plan) reads a mutable PostgreSQL table that a lab member edits by hand, so it is refreshed about as often as the services panel

traces.provenance: chosen 2026-09-24 - collect_traces.py (Phase 3) reads OpenObserve over HTTP; kept short like identity rather than long like mcp_live, since a single-node OpenObserve answering `_search` on its own disk is cheap, unlike `claude mcp list` reaching 28 remote servers

subprocess_default.provenance: chosen - R10, every subprocess call carries an explicit timeout

mcp_list.provenance: chosen - it reaches 28 servers over the network; a timeout is reported as unavailable with the reason, never as an empty roster

action_default.provenance: chosen - install.ps1 and the offline suite both run for minutes

ping.provenance: chosen - the launcher asks /api/ping on loopback before binding; nothing legitimate on 127.0.0.1 takes longer, and a slow answer must not delay the refusal

openobserve_ingest.provenance: chosen 2026-09-24 - rt_actions.py's second sink sits on the hot path of every dashboard action, so a wedged OpenObserve must not delay the action's own response by more than this before the JSONL fallback is reported as the only record

openobserve_search.provenance: chosen 2026-09-24 - collect_traces.py's read side; longer than the ingest timeout because a _search query over a retained stream costs more than a single-record insert

voice_ask_wait.unit: seconds the /api/voice/ask route blocks waiting for the daemon's answer file before giving up
voice_ask_wait.provenance: measured 2026-09-26 - the original 20 s timed out before any answer could arrive: daemon-config.json records a 36.991 s median writer-role call, and the resident ornith:9b-gpu decoded at 20.3 tok/s that day. Kept just under the daemon's own ask_request_ttl_s (90 s) so the dashboard never waits on a request the daemon has already expired. Since 2026-10-02 (plan2, voice-graph-lookup) this is a PER-PART wait, not a single total: the vault part and the graph part (plan1b) each get up to this long since their own last published part, so a slow graph query does not cut off a vault answer that already arrived

usage_window_days.unit: days of transcript history summed for the week bar
usage_window_days.provenance: chosen 2026-09-01 - the operator asked for a WEEK bar, and a week is what the subscription limit is stated in

usage_scan_bytes.unit: bytes read from ONE transcript before the scan gives up on it and says so
usage_scan_bytes.provenance: chosen - this collector reads transcripts WHOLE rather than by tail, so an unbounded read is a page that hangs on the largest session anyone has ever had

outbox_listed.unit: outbox entries named in the snapshot before the rest are only counted
outbox_listed.provenance: chosen 2026-09-01 - the operator asked to SEE what is waiting to be written, and a list read on hover is read standing up

voice_question_chars.provenance: chosen 2026-09-26 - a spoken question this long is almost certainly a transcription runaway, not a real question; refused rather than truncated, matching inbox_message_chars

flow_groups.unit: tool groups drawn around one agent before the rest become a count
flow_groups.provenance: measured 2026-09-01 - at seven, a session that had used more than seven distinct tools lost the ones it had used least recently, and Write went missing from a session that had just written a file

flow_subagents.unit: subagent dispatches kept for one session, counted apart from its steps
flow_subagents.provenance: measured 2026-09-01 - a dispatch sharing the step list vanished behind 120 later Bash calls, so the one thing being looked for was the one thing the cap dropped

flow_hooks_per_event.unit: hook firings kept PER EVENT, so a once-per-session hook is not evicted by a once-per-tool-call one
flow_hooks_per_event.provenance: measured 2026-09-01 - PreToolUse and PostToolUse fire on every tool call, so a flat last-N window held nothing but those two and the operator never saw RTK or caveman, which fire at SessionStart

flow_hooks.unit: hook firings kept for one session, counted apart from its steps
flow_hooks.provenance: measured 2026-09-01 - PreToolUse and PostToolUse fire on EVERY tool call, so hooks sharing the step list would drown the flow they are meant to explain

flow_steps.unit: steps of one session's flow kept for the Real-Time Process tab
flow_steps.provenance: chosen - the tab answers what is happening NOW, and a transcript tail carries far more than anyone reads standing up

prompt_chars.unit: characters of a session's current prompt
prompt_chars.provenance: chosen - the fleet reads sessions across every project on this machine, one of them a litigation matter, so prompts are truncated before they reach the page

inbox_message_chars.provenance: chosen - a message longer than this is refused rather than truncated, because a truncated instruction delivered as whole is the failure mode the local-model window rules already legislate against

output_tail_chars.unit: characters kept from the END of an action's stdout and stderr
output_tail_chars.provenance: specified - outbox_io.tail's rule: a Python traceback names its exception on the LAST line while its opening frames are identical on every failure, so truncation keeps the tail

transcript_tail_bytes.unit: bytes read from the end of a session transcript
transcript_tail_bytes.provenance: chosen - a transcript grows without bound and only its tail carries current state

traces_max_pages.unit: pages read from OpenObserve before the collector stops and reports a bound rather than reading forever (R10)
traces_max_pages.provenance: chosen 2026-09-24 - 500 rows is enough for a panel read standing up; a deeper history belongs to OpenObserve's own UI, not this one

session_idle.unit: seconds without a new transcript record before a session is drawn as waiting
session_idle.provenance: chosen - the harness emits no explicit idle event, so waiting is inferred from silence, and a threshold shorter than a long tool call would report a working session as idle

graph_snapshot.provenance: chosen - a graph snapshot older than a day is rendered stale rather than current, because refreshing it costs a local-writer dispatch and nobody does it hourly

green_stamp.provenance: chosen - a week-old green stamp is still green, but it is shown as aged so 'green from three days ago' is never read as 'green now'

daemon_lock.provenance: chosen - passed to vault_lock.held_by_live_holder as its staleness ceiling; a lock older than this with a dead holder is reported not-running

daemon_lock_boot_skew_tolerance.provenance: chosen 2026-10-07, mirrors obsidian-cli/daemon-config.json's lock.boot_skew_tolerance_s (PR #42 review, Medium M2): passed to the same held_by_live_holder call so this panel's own liveness read applies the identical clock-skew margin the daemon's own lock acquisition uses, rather than reporting a momentary false not-running right after a clock correction near boot

excluded_projects.provenance: chosen - empty by default; add a project directory name here and no session from it reaches the page at all
excluded_projects.note: Exclusion is applied before truncation, not after, so an excluded project contributes nothing rather than a shortened something.

engine.provenance: chosen 2026-09-26 - the Devoir2 reference implementation's proven baseline (voice_input_node.py); the Whisper variant is chosen by measurement, see model_size

model_size.provenance: chosen by the operator 2026-09-26 from a scored comparison of small/float16, medium, large-v3-turbo and large-v3 (int8_float16) on the operator's 3 dictated recordings (6MIG841-Lab CommandeVocale/CommandeAccepte/CommandeFausse, scored against the operator's own reference text, not Devoir2's constants, which are Whisper small's own output), each candidate in a fresh process beside the resident writer-role model. Score = (100 - word error %) and live-caption speed (100 when a 19.5 s buffer transcribes within partial_refresh_ms) averaged, gated on demoting at most 10% of the LLM from VRAM: large-v3-turbo 98.8 (2.5% WER, 0.74 s, 945 MiB dedicated, 7% of the LLM demoted), small 95.0 (10.0% WER, 0.58 s, 625 MiB, 2%), medium 86.6 (7.5%, 1.24 s), large-v3 gated out (2.5%, 1.69 s, 1617 MiB, 24% of the LLM demoted). Sample is 40 reference words, so one word is 2.5% WER

compute_type.provenance: measured 2026-09-26 in the same comparison as model_size: int8 weights with float16 compute keep large-v3-turbo at 945 MiB dedicated beside the resident writer-role model, which demoted 385 MiB of the LLM and delayed its next answer by 0.20 s (2.48 s -> 2.68 s on a short prompt)

device.provenance: chosen by the operator 2026-09-26 ('no CPU, all on GPU') - matches Devoir2's speech_device=cuda. Needs the NVIDIA runtime of requirements-voice-cuda.txt on a machine without a system CUDA Toolkit. Nothing larger than Whisper small fits beside the resident writer-role model without WDDM demoting part of the LLM to system RAM (measured 2026-09-26, per-process GPU Process Memory counters)

language.provenance: chosen 2026-09-26 - the per-request voice-panel dropdown (auto/en/fr) governs; this stays null as the fallback default when a caller omits language entirely

vad_filter.provenance: copied 2026-09-26 from Devoir2 (devoir2.transcription.vad_filtre), which measured Whisper transcribing silence and pure tones as subtitle credits; the live preview re-transcribes a buffer that is mostly silence before speech starts

vad_min_silence_ms.provenance: copied 2026-09-26 from Devoir2 (vad_duree_silence_min_ms): short against a thinking pause, long against a breath

condition_on_previous_text.provenance: copied 2026-09-26 from Devoir2 (conditionner_sur_texte_precedent): stops one hallucination from repeating at every live-preview refresh

partial_refresh_ms.provenance: measured 2026-09-26 - Whisper small/float16 on cuda transcribed a 6.4 s sentence in 0.51-0.71 s beside the resident writer model; re-checked the same day for large-v3-turbo int8_float16, which transcribes a 19.5 s buffer in 0.74 s (median of 5), so 1 s still keeps the caption live. Devoir2's 3.0 s was sized for its CPU cost of 1.44 s, and the page's in-flight guard makes the real cadence max(this, one transcription) so previews never overlap

answer_poll_ms.provenance: chosen 2026-10-02 at the voice-graph-lookup design review (docs/superpowers/plans/2026-10-02-voice-graph-lookup/spec.md section 7): fast enough that a held-P push-to-talk turn does not feel stalled, matching the existing daemon.ask_poll_interval_s=1s cadence on the daemon's own side

action_log.provenance: chosen - append-only, the same shape as vault_journal.py, outside the repository so it is never committed

inbox_root.provenance: chosen - beside the obsidian outbox, under ~/.claude and therefore outside the vault, so vault-access-guard.py is not involved

graph_snapshot.provenance: chosen - written by local-writer, read by the dashboard. Deliberately NOT inside graphify-out/, which vault-access-guard.py refuses to every caller but local-writer

obsidian_outbox.provenance: specified - the outbox layout owned by the obsidian-cli skill; its singleton lock sits beside it as obsidian-outbox.lock
obsidian_outbox.note: Read for liveness and queue DEPTH only, never for note content. It is under the Claude home and therefore outside the vault, so vault-access-guard.py is not involved and the single-writer rule is untouched.

daemon_singleton_lock.provenance: specified - daemon_outbox.py singleton_lock(), which names vault-daemon.lock beside the outbox
daemon_singleton_lock.note: This is the SINGLETON lock and it is NOT the write lock. obsidian-outbox.lock, in the same directory, serializes writers and is held only for the instant of a write, so asking IT whether a daemon is running answers no on a healthy machine. Measured 2026-08-30: this collector asked the write lock first and reported a running daemon as dead, which is the exact backwards reading the obsidian-cli suite warns about.
